chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the man who has a number of [missed] fasts upon him from the month of Ramadan, does he fast optional [fasts]? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'No, until he makes up for what is upon him from the month of Ramadan.'

key_terms.طَائِفَةٌ: A number or portion (referring to missed fasts)
key_terms.يَقْضِيَ: He makes up / fulfills the obligation

ai.seo_question: Can I fast voluntary fasts if I still have missed Ramadan fasts to make up?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the priority of obligatory debt (qada) over voluntary worship (nafl), establishing that missed Ramadan fasts must be settled before one engages in supererogatory fasting. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that fulfilling one's primary religious duties takes precedence over additional acts of devotion, ensuring the integrity of the obligatory fast is maintained first.
